answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pods for a four-player game. 2. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, and 1 additional Adult per player (so 7 Adults total with four players) in the Intruder bag.
answers.evidence: Board setup steps 7 and 10: 3 pods for 3–4 players; lowest-numbered in A, next in B then alternate; all Locked. Intruder bag list specifies base tokens plus one Adult per player.

answers.answer: 1. Remove from both Corporate and Personal decks all Objectives showing a player count above the actual count, shuffle the two decks separately, and deal each player one of each, hidden. 2. At the First Encounter—the first time an Intruder miniature appears—each player immediately chooses one of their two cards; remove the rejected card face down without looking at it. 3. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence: Crew setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments: First Encounter.

answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself and two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. 2. Contamination cards cannot pay any Action cost. 3. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions: Action Cost and Actions from Action cards.

answers.answer: 1. After finishing their own round, the Character suffers 1 Light Wound for ending the round in a burning Room. 2. Having passed, they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase, though the FAQ allows an Interruption after passing. 3. When passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not cause this Character to take Fire damage again that turn; the Fire wound is assessed at the end of that Character's own round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Player rounds; Fire markers.

answers.answer: 1. On entering, flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then remove the token to the box. Set the Room's Item count by rotating the tile so the token's number faces the board's Item Counter (except Nest and Slime Room). 2. Resolve the Exploration effect: Silence cancels the Noise roll, Danger resolves as Danger instead of a roll, and other listed symbols apply their effect. 3. If the destination has no Characters or Intruders, make a Noise roll; skip the roll if either is already there. 4. A numbered result places Noise in the matching connected Corridor; Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders in, or, if none are eligible, places Noise in each empty connected Corridor. Silence does nothing. Slime makes Silence resolve as Danger.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2. It follows normal movement restrictions and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing one Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. 3. It is forbidden in Combat and when every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. 4. Closed Doors block passage. 5. A miniature cannot stop in a Corridor; characters and Intruders occupy Rooms only.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: 1. A numbered roll that calls for a Corridor already containing Noise triggers an Encounter instead of placing another marker. 2. Resolve the Encounter by removing all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if it has an Entrance), drawing a bag token, and placing its matching Intruder in the Room (unless it is Blank). 3. Keep a drawn non-Blank token set aside outside the bag; it can return if that Intruder later hides in Technical Corridors. A Noise marker for a Technical Corridors Entrance goes on the shared Technical Corridors space. 4. Compare the token number with the triggering player's hand size, counting both Action and Contamination cards: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack. Contamination cards do count for this comparison.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters.

answers.answer: 1. Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character into the Room, not just one. 2. If none are eligible (none neighboring, or all in Combat), place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors when the Room has an Entrance. 3. Intruder movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; the Intruder and Character are simply in Combat. 4. A Slime marker turns a Silence result into Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens: Danger; Noise roll: Danger; Encounters; Slime marker.

answers.answer: 1. On a Blank drawn during an Encounter, put a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without placing an Intruder. 2. Only if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if one is available. 3. In bag development, a Blank adds an Adult token if available and then the Blank is returned to the bag; this is not conditional on it being the last token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: Blank token; Event Phase: Intruder bag development, Blank.

answers.answer: 1. When Intruders trying to move together meet the same Closed Door, they destroy it and all stay in their original Room. 2. The Door token becomes lying (Destroyed); movement through it is allowed, but it can never be Closed again (except by Plasma Torch). 3. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked; it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers: Door tokens; FAQ Rounds, events, damage and Intruders.

answers.answer: 1. When an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, remove its miniature from the board, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. 2. Noise on the shared Technical Corridors space remains. 3. Characters cannot normally use Technical Corridors, with exceptions for the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item. 4. Door tokens cannot be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: 1. Shoot costs 1 Action card, requires a Weapon in Hand with Ammo, targets one Intruder in your Room, and discards 1 Ammo before rolling the Combat die. It does not add Contamination. A blank misses without a Melee penalty; the die's two-hit result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting, before Weapon modifications. 2. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card onto the top of your Action discard pile, targets one Intruder in your Room, and rolls the Combat die. A miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound; a two-hit result counts as only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Combat: Shoot and Melee Attack.

answers.answer: 1. After damage, add Injury markers and check against the Intruder's total current Injuries. A Larva dies at 1 Injury; an Adult requires drawing one Intruder Attack card and dies if its blood value is no greater than its Injuries; a Queen requires drawing two cards and dies if their summed blood is no greater than its Injuries. 2. On a Queen's death, remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room. 3. If either card in the Queen's check has a Retreat arrow, retreat happens instead of a numerical death check: draw an Event card and move the Queen through the Corridor matching its Intruder movement number, then discard that Event card; no death/Carcass is specified for retreat.
answers.evidence: Combat: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with larger types (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). 2. Each attack targets the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to escape from. 3. If they survive, they complete the move to the neighboring Room and resolve normal entry effects: explore if unexplored and make a Noise roll if the destination is empty.
answers.evidence: Combat: Character Escape; Intruder Attack.

answers.answer: 1. With several Characters in the Room, target the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; break a tie by the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. 2. Draw one Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder symbol means resolve its effect; otherwise it misses. Ignore the blood icon during an attack. 3. For a Larva, do not draw an Attack card: move the Larva miniature to the target's Character board and give the target 1 Contamination card. 4. Put that Contamination card on top of the target's Action discard pile. If they already have a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva stays, and they still gain the Contamination card without automatically dying.
answers.evidence: Combat: Intruder Attack and Infest; Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: 1. Dressing a Serious Wound does not prevent death from a further Wound when the Character already has 3 Serious Wounds; they die upon suffering any additional Wound, including Light. 2. Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the effect specifies. 4. On death, place the Character Corpse token in the Room as a Character Corpse Object and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death.

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand; they remove all non-Infected scanned cards, while an Infected result places a Larva on the board (if one was already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room). Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes Slime. 2. Surgery scans every Contamination card across deck, hand, and discard, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva from the Character board if present. 3. Surgery then inflicts 1 Light Wound and automatically passes; shuffle all cards, including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards, into the Action deck. The hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen, Surgery, Shower Room; Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: 1. In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee against them; each Injury destroys one Egg. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov destroys 1, and they may be thrown at a Room with Eggs as if an Intruder were there. 2. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound; whether a successful Egg Melee causes Contamination is unsupported by the summary, which says the manual wording does not settle it. 3. Make a Noise roll after every single attempt to destroy an Egg. Fire in a Room with uncarried Eggs destroys one Egg during each Fire Damage step. 4. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest explicitly say the successful Egg Melee Contamination case is not uniquely resolved; other Egg destruction procedures are specified.

answers.answer: 1. To enter, use the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); the Pod must be Unlocked with an open Character space, and neither an Intruder nor a Malfunction may be in the Section. First make a Noise roll; if an Intruder appears or is present, entry fails. 2. A Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character spaces. 3. After boarding, you may launch immediately. If you wait, you pass the current turn and remain present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose to keep waiting and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and take a full round of 2 Actions. A second Character boarding a waiting Pod may launch immediately with both aboard; if an Intruder appears in the Section while you wait, all Pod occupants return to the Room. A Malfunction while waiting does not prevent waiting, launching, or exiting, but blocks new Pod entry.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods.

answers.answer: 1. Check in order: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2. If two Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders; already-launched Pod passengers are away and remain eligible for checks. 3. If the ship is not headed to Earth, hibernating Characters die at the Coordinates check, except a Character with Quarantine survives hibernation if the destination is Mars. 4. At Contamination check, scan the survivor's cards in hand, deck, and discard; if any is Infected, shuffle all their cards and draw four, dying if any of the four is a Contamination card. A Larva triggers the shuffle-and-four test directly. 5. Pod passengers do need the Contamination check: the summary says each surviving Character, whether hibernating or evacuated, checks Contamination.
answers.evidence: Victory Check (run if at least 1 Character survived — hibernating or escaped).
